meta.title: General Roman Calendar for Saint of the Day
meta.status: Ready on this side only. Do not send to Grok Build and do not publish until Michael says.
meta.basis: Roman Missal, Third Typical Edition (2002), reprint of 2008, with later additions through the decree on Saint John Henry Newman (signed 9 November 2025, published 3 February 2026).
meta.nameStyle: English Roman Missal style, already used by the live site GRC module and the /saints library: ‘Saint’ and ‘Saints’ written out, not ‘St’ or ‘St.’ British spelling.
meta.slugStyle: slug is the A–Z /saints library id (for example f-saint-francis-of-assisi), used as the hash on /journeys/saints. figureSlug is the smaller encyclopedia figure page, when one exists. slugs is used when one celebration covers more than one library page.
meta.fallbackRule: On a feria (no GRC celebration that day), keep the site’s current Saint of the Day pick: the England and Wales proper if the live today-strip would show one, otherwise the existing martyrology saint. Do not treat an England and Wales proper as a General Roman Calendar celebration.
sources: Live /saints library in the site bundle, and the letter JSON snapshot under /workspace/site-images/work/json/
Site source: src/data/saint-of-the-day.ts, day-celebration.ts, martyrology.ts, today-strip.tsx
Calendarium Romanum Generale in the Roman Missal, editio typica tertia (2008 reprint)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Roman_Calendar (English Missal names, with citations to the decrees)

Vatican decrees: Mother of the Church (11 Feb 2018); Paul VI (25 Jan 2019); Our Lady of Loreto (31 Oct 2019); Faustina (18 May 2020); Martha, Mary and Lazarus (26 Jan 2021); Gregory of Narek, John of Ávila and Hildegard (25 Jan 2021); Irenaeus, Doctor (21 Jan 2022); Teresa of Calcutta (11 Feb 2025); John Henry Newman, Priest and Doctor of the Church (decree 9 Nov 2025, published 3 Feb 2026)

moveable.name: Ash Wednesday
moveable.rule: 46 days before Easter (Wednesday before the First Sunday of Lent)

moveable.name: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord
Good Friday of the Passion of the Lord
Easter Sunday of the Resurrection of the Lord
moveable.rule: Sunday after the first full moon on or after 21 March (Gregorian Computus, as in the site calendar)

moveable.name: Second Sunday of Easter, or of Divine Mercy
moveable.rule: Sunday after Easter (the octave day of Easter)

moveable.name: The Ascension of the Lord
moveable.rule: Thursday, 39 days after Easter (the fortieth day counting Easter). In some particular calendars it is transferred to the following Sunday; England and Wales keep the Thursday.

moveable.name: Pentecost Sunday
moveable.rule: Sunday, 49 days after Easter (the fiftieth day counting Easter)

moveable.name: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church
moveable.rule: Monday after Pentecost. If this Memorial coincides with another obligatory Memorial, only Mother of the Church is kept that year (Notification, 24 March 2018).
moveable.note: Added to the General Roman Calendar by decree of 11 February 2018. Missing from the live site grc-calendar module.

moveable.name: The Most Holy Trinity
moveable.rule: Sunday after Pentecost (56 days after Easter)

moveable.name: The Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ
moveable.rule: Thursday after Trinity (60 days after Easter; 11 days after Pentecost). Particular calendars, including England and Wales, may keep it on the following Sunday.

moveable.name: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
moveable.rule: Friday after the Second Sunday after Pentecost (68 days after Easter; 19 days after Pentecost)

moveable.name: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary
moveable.rule: Saturday after the Sacred Heart (69 days after Easter; 20 days after Pentecost). If it coincides with another obligatory Memorial, both are optional that year.

moveable.name: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
moveable.rule: Last Sunday in Ordinary Time: the Sunday before the First Sunday of Advent

moveable.name: First Sunday of Advent
moveable.rule: Four Sundays before 25 December. If Christmas is a Sunday, Advent starts 28 days earlier; otherwise 21 days plus the weekday number of Christmas (Sunday = 0).

moveable.name: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph
moveable.rule: Sunday within the Octave of Christmas, or 30 December if there is no such Sunday (when Christmas itself is a Sunday)
moveable.note: In 2027 this falls on 26 December, so the Feast of Saint Stephen is impeded that year.

moveable.name: The Baptism of the Lord
moveable.rule: Sunday after 6 January. If the Epiphany is transferred to Sunday 7 or 8 January, the Baptism is kept on the following Monday.

solemnityTransfers.name: The Annunciation of the Lord
solemnityTransfers.rule: If 25 March falls in Holy Week or the Octave of Easter, transfer to the Monday after the Octave of Easter.

englandAndWales.note: Do not mix these into the General Roman Calendar. This is an optional national list only.
